title: Build changelog stewardship playbook and rapid review gates
creator: Ariana Patel
description: Create a lightweight, repeatable playbook and signoff flow for changelogs that supports both internal ops readiness and customer-facing micro-changelogs. The playbook should define roles (author, reviewer, shepherd), embargo rules, escalation paths for ambiguous items, templates for two audience tiers (developer & enterprise), and a rapid-review gate for high-frequency patch releases. Outcome: reduce review cycle time by 30% and eliminate last-minute redactions for enterprise customers.
acceptance_criteria: One-page playbook draft published in Confluence with clear role definitions and daily owner rotation guidance
Two changelog templates created: developer-facing (concise) and enterprise-facing (impact + mitigation + SLO notes)
Automated notification flow configured in Slack (channel + @changelog-shepherd ping) and verified in a dry run
Signoff matrix with named owners for legal/security/ops created and validated by representatives
A pilot run completed for the console-2025.09 patch and metrics captured for time-to-signoff
comments: 2025-09-02 Ariana Patel: Kickoff - scoped playbook to cover embargo handling and two templates. Asked design for micro-copy options and asked Legal to list redaction triggers.
2025-09-03 Jamal Rivera: Rapid-review gate proposal: 4-hour SLAs for patch changes, shepherd rotates weekly. Posted initial flow diagram in Confluence and requested feedback from Ops.
2025-09-04 Sofia Klein (Design): Shared 3 micro-copy options for developer template; recommended a 3-line summary + bullets for affected APIs. Link to artboard provided.
2025-09-05 Marcus Chen (Eng): Raised concern about distribution of embargoed notes across regions; suggested adding regional readiness checklist and a deploy-block dependency (ENG-50921).

2025-09-06 Evelyn Ortiz (Legal): Provided redaction guidelines and flagged authentication/PII-change language as requiring explicit legal signoff. Requested review window up to 24 hours for sensitive items.

2025-09-07 Jamal Rivera: Incorporated legal feedback; adjusted rapid-review gate to allow a 24-hour legal window for sensitive items and 4-hour for non-sensitive. Drafted signoff matrix and assigned initial shepherds.
2025-09-08 Priya Nair (Support): Requested inclusion of 'customer-facing mitigation steps' section for Enterprise template. Added example mitigation copy and updated acceptance criteria.

2025-09-09 Ariana Patel: Ran dry-run with console-2025.09 pre-release slice. Time-to-signoff measured 6 hours (target 8). Noted friction: unclear owner for data-migration notes; follow-up action to assign to infra lead. Created follow-up ticket ENG-84712.
decisions: Adopt two-tier templates (developer / enterprise) rather than a single universal template to reduce unnecessary detail for developers
Introduce 'Shepherd' role that owns day-of coordination and pings legal/ops when an item is flagged
Use Slack workflow to surface changes automatically and create a lightweight audit trail (rather than heavier email flows)
Embed quick links in the changelog draft to the runbook and incident dashboard for ops readiness checks
open_risks: Legal review could introduce delays for sensitive items, possibly exceeding targeted SLA for rapid patches
Regional rollout differences (comms windows and legal/regulatory carve-outs) will require per-region owners—resourcing gap currently
External partner integrations (marketplace partners) may require separate redaction and signoff rules not yet modeled
next_steps: Finalize Confluence playbook v1 and tag stakeholders for approval (due 2025-09-12)
Run a second pilot with a service-level patch that includes a data-migration note (target week of 2025-09-15)
Create onboarding checklist for rotating Shepherds and publish to #changelog-shepherd channel
Work with Engineering to add a changelog metadata flag in the release pipeline so items can be auto-classified as 'sensitive' or 'non-sensitive'
